## 

```{r library}
library(tidyverse)
library(readxl)
library(janitor)

```

```{r import temocillin data}
# Raw CHEQS extract is only available on the hospital network machine, so the
# original import is kept here for provenance but not run on this machine.
# Temocillin_CHEQS <- read_excel("~/R_Projects/CUH_Abx_review/Raw_data/Temocillin/Temocillin_CHEQS.xlsx") %>%
#   clean_names() %>%
#   filter(!is.na(zone_size))%>% # clear empty panels from testing other MICs
#   group_by(specimen_number, susc_test_meth) %>% #keep last record per EUCAST or MIC per specimen
#   slice(which.max(last_verified)) %>%
#   ungroup()

# Instead, load the already-processed (pivoted) panel-level data saved from
# that pipeline, so this document can run standalone from temocillin_data.rds.
Panels <- readRDS("temocillin_data.rds")
```

```{r filter organisms of interest}
# Restrict to E. coli (excluding mixed-growth and the O157 serotype),
# Klebsiella spp. (excluding aerogenes), and Proteus mirabilis, and to
# samples with both an EUCAST and an MIC (Etest) result recorded (Both == 1).
organisms_of_interest <- Panels %>%
  filter(
    organism_or_component == "ESCHERICHIA COLI [202]" |
      (str_detect(organism_or_component, "^KLEBSIELLA") &
         !str_detect(organism_or_component, "AEROGENES")) |
      organism_or_component == "PROTEUS MIRABILIS [338]"
  ) %>%
  filter(Both == 1) %>%
  mutate(organism = organism_or_component %>%
           str_remove("\\s*\\[\\d+\\]$") %>%
           str_to_sentence(),
         # Etest MIC (mg/L): strip </> qualifiers and ceiling at 256
         MIC = `zone_size_M ETEST` %>%
           str_remove_all("[<>]") %>%
           as.numeric() %>%
           pmin(256),
         EUCAST = as.numeric(`zone_size_M EUCAST`),
         # Re-derive S/I/R from the raw zone size / MIC using the EUCAST
         # v16.1 temocillin breakpoints documented in CLAUDE.md (zone: S>=50,
         # R<17; MIC: S<=0.001, R>16), rather than relying on the recorded
         # susceptibility_M EUCAST / susceptibility_M ETEST fields (which
         # have a few gaps/edge cases). Downstream tables use these new
         # columns but keep the original "EUCAST" / "Etest" labelling.
         EUCAST_interp = case_when(
           is.na(EUCAST) ~ NA_character_,
           EUCAST < 17 ~ "R",
           EUCAST < 50 ~ "I",
           TRUE ~ "S"
         ),
         ETEST_interp = case_when(
           is.na(MIC) ~ NA_character_,
           MIC > 16 ~ "R",
           MIC > 0.001 ~ "I",
           TRUE ~ "S"
         ),
         # collapse Klebsiella species for plotting (keeps the 3-colour palette)
         organism_group = if_else(str_detect(organism, "^Klebsiella"),
                                   "Klebsiella spp.", organism),
         # match status between the re-interpreted EUCAST and Etest calls
         match_status = case_when(
           EUCAST_interp == ETEST_interp ~ "Agreement",
           EUCAST_interp == "I" & ETEST_interp == "R" ~ "I to R",
           EUCAST_interp == "R" & ETEST_interp == "I" ~ "R to I"
         ))
```

```{r MIC vs EUCAST scatter}
# EUCAST R/I cutoffs from CLAUDE.md: disc zone 17mm, MIC 16 mg/L. (The S
# cutoffs, zone >=50mm / MIC <=0.001 mg/L, fall outside the achievable data
# range and aren't shown.)
organisms_of_interest %>%
  mutate(match_status = factor(match_status, levels = c("Agreement", "I to R", "R to I"))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = EUCAST, y = MIC, color = match_status)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 17, linetype = "dashed", color = "#898781") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 16, linetype = "dashed", color = "#898781") +
  annotate("text", x = 17, y = 256, label = "17mm", hjust = -0.1, size = 3, color = "#52514e") +
  annotate("text", x = 5, y = 16, label = "16 mg/L", vjust = -0.5, size = 3, color = "#52514e") +
  geom_count(alpha = 0.75) +
  scale_y_log10(breaks = c(0.032, 0.064, 0.25, 1, 4, 16, 64, 256),
                labels = c("0.032", "0.064", "0.25", "1", "4", "16", "64", "≥256")) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 40, 5)) +
  # status colour: green = agreement, amber/red = the two discordant directions
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Agreement" = "#0ca30c",
                                 "I to R" = "#fab219",
                                 "R to I" = "#d03b3b")) +
  labs(x = "EUCAST disc zone diameter (mm)",
       y = "Etest MIC (mg/L, log scale)",
       color = "EUCAST vs Etest", size = "Count",
       title = "MIC vs EUCAST zone diameter") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        legend.position = "right")
```

```{r specimen type by organism crosstab}
library(gt)

organisms_of_interest %>%
  count(specimen_type, organism, .drop = FALSE) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = organism, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) %>%
  mutate(Total = rowSums(across(where(is.numeric)))) %>%
  gt(rowname_col = "specimen_type") %>%
  tab_header(title = "Specimen type by organism",
             subtitle = "E. coli, Klebsiella spp. (excl. aerogenes), and Proteus mirabilis") %>%
  tab_stubhead(label = "Specimen type") %>%
  grand_summary_rows(columns = everything(),
                      fns = list(Total = ~ sum(.)),
                      fmt = ~ fmt_integer(.)) %>%
  tab_style(style = cell_text(weight = "bold"),
            locations = cells_body(columns = Total)) %>%
  tab_options(table.font.size = px(13))
```

Data extracted from CHEQS - Microbiology results. Result filters set to date from 01/01/2023 to 21/10/26, and component to "TEMOCILLIN\|TEMGN"

There are 19902 individual temocillin records from 18985 specimens and 12498 patients.

```{r comparison table}

# Panels is already pivoted (one row per specimen/organism with ETEST,
# EUCAST and Both flags) in temocillin_data.rds, so no further reshaping
# is needed here.

Panels %>%
  summarise(n = n(),
            `MIC and disc` = sum(Both),
            .by = specimen_type)
  
```

```{r discordance check overall}
library(gt)

lvl <- c("S", "I", "R")

# Overall categorical agreement for the inclusion-criteria cohort (E. coli,
# Klebsiella spp. excl. aerogenes, Proteus mirabilis; Both == 1), with no
# breakdown by specimen type or organism. Uses EUCAST_interp / ETEST_interp
# (zone/MIC re-interpreted against the CLAUDE.md breakpoints).
xtab_overall <- organisms_of_interest %>%
  mutate(across(c(EUCAST_interp, ETEST_interp), ~ factor(.x, levels = lvl))) %>%
  count(EUCAST_interp, ETEST_interp, .drop = FALSE) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = ETEST_interp,
              names_prefix = "ETEST:",
              values_from = n,
              values_fill = 0)

xtab_overall %>%
  arrange(EUCAST_interp) %>%
  gt(rowname_col = "EUCAST_interp") %>%
  tab_header(title = "Categorical agreement: EUCAST vs Etest",
             subtitle = "Overall — both results present (n = 613)") %>%
  tab_stubhead(label = "EUCAST") %>%
  cols_label_with(fn = ~ sub("ETEST:", "", .x)) %>%
  tab_spanner(label = "Etest", columns = starts_with("ETEST:")) %>%
  # shade the agreement diagonal
  tab_style(style = cell_fill(color = "#E8F4EA"),
            locations = list(
              cells_body(columns = `ETEST:S`, rows = EUCAST_interp == "S"),
              cells_body(columns = `ETEST:I`, rows = EUCAST_interp == "I"),
              cells_body(columns = `ETEST:R`, rows = EUCAST_interp == "R"))) %>%
  # flag very major errors (EUCAST R, Etest S)
  tab_style(style = list(cell_fill(color = "#F8D7DA"), cell_text(weight = "bold")),
            locations = cells_body(columns = `ETEST:S`,
                                   rows = EUCAST_interp == "R")) %>%
  # I <-> R mismatches (minor errors)
  tab_style(style = cell_fill(color = "#F8D7DA"),
            locations = list(
              cells_body(columns = `ETEST:R`, rows = EUCAST_interp == "I"),
              cells_body(columns = `ETEST:I`, rows = EUCAST_interp == "R"))) %>%
  grand_summary_rows(columns = starts_with("ETEST:"),
                      fns = list(Total = ~ sum(.)),
                      fmt = ~ fmt_integer(.))
```

## Agreement summary

```{r agreement summary setup}
# Categorical agreement, and I<->R category changes, for the
# inclusion-criteria cohort (Both == 1), using EUCAST_interp / ETEST_interp
# (zone/MIC re-interpreted against the CLAUDE.md breakpoints).
# Re-deriving from the raw zone size/MIC recovers samples that had a zone
# size but no recorded EUCAST susceptibility call, so this denominator can
# be larger than when using the recorded fields directly.
summarise_agreement <- function(df) {
  df %>%
    filter(!is.na(EUCAST_interp), !is.na(ETEST_interp)) %>%
    summarise(
      n = n(),
      `Agreement, n (%)` = sprintf("%d (%.1f%%)",
                                    sum(EUCAST_interp == ETEST_interp),
                                    100 * mean(EUCAST_interp == ETEST_interp)),
      `I to R, n (%)` = sprintf("%d (%.1f%%)",
                                 sum(EUCAST_interp == "I" & ETEST_interp == "R"),
                                 100 * mean(EUCAST_interp == "I" & ETEST_interp == "R")),
      `R to I, n (%)` = sprintf("%d (%.1f%%)",
                                 sum(EUCAST_interp == "R" & ETEST_interp == "I"),
                                 100 * mean(EUCAST_interp == "R" & ETEST_interp == "I")),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
}

excluded_n <- nrow(organisms_of_interest) -
  sum(!is.na(organisms_of_interest$EUCAST_interp) &
        !is.na(organisms_of_interest$ETEST_interp))
```

```{r agreement summary overall}
tbl_agreement_overall <- organisms_of_interest %>%
  summarise_agreement() %>%
  gt() %>%
  tab_header(title = "Agreement summary", subtitle = "Overall") %>%
  cols_label(n = "n (valid pairs)") %>%
  tab_options(table.font.size = px(13))

if (excluded_n > 0) {
  tbl_agreement_overall <- tbl_agreement_overall %>%
    tab_footnote(footnote = paste0(excluded_n, " sample(s) excluded: zone size/MIC not recorded."))
}

tbl_agreement_overall
```

## Zone diameter distribution (full dataset)

```{r zone diameter full dataset setup}
# Unlike the rest of the report, this uses the FULL dataset (all organisms,
# not just the E. coli/Klebsiella/Proteus inclusion criteria), to see how
# the EUCAST disc zone diameter is distributed across every specimen type
# and organism recorded. Drops 37 rows with no recorded zone and the 3 rows
# with a physically impossible zone (81/223/230mm, almost certainly
# data-entry typos, as found in the earlier breakpoint QC check).
#
# Organisms with very small counts are amalgamated to genus level: the
# single "E. coli type O157" row folds into Escherichia coli (same species,
# different serotype); "Klebsiella sp" (n=2, unspecified species) becomes
# its own small "Klebsiella spp." group; the single mixed-growth "E. coli /
# Hafnia alvei" row (two different genera) goes to "Other / mixed growth"
# rather than being forced into either genus. Klebsiella oxytoca,
# pneumoniae and variicola, Proteus mirabilis and Coliform bacilli all have
# enough samples (>=120) to stand alone.
Panels_zone <- Panels %>%
  mutate(EUCAST_zone = as.numeric(`zone_size_M EUCAST`)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(EUCAST_zone), EUCAST_zone <= 50) %>%
  mutate(
    organism_group_full = case_when(
      str_detect(organism_or_component, "HAFNIA ALVEI") ~ "Other / mixed growth",
      str_detect(organism_or_component, "^ESCHERICHIA COLI") ~ "Escherichia coli",
      organism_or_component == "KLEBSIELLA PNEUMONIAE [254]" ~ "Klebsiella pneumoniae",
      organism_or_component == "KLEBSIELLA OXYTOCA [253]" ~ "Klebsiella oxytoca",
      organism_or_component == "KLEBSIELLA VARIICOLA [909]" ~ "Klebsiella variicola",
      organism_or_component == "KLEBSIELLA SP [908]" ~ "Klebsiella spp. (other)",
      organism_or_component == "PROTEUS MIRABILIS [338]" ~ "Proteus mirabilis",
      organism_or_component == "COLIFORM BACILLI [779]" ~ "Coliform bacilli"
    )
  )
```

```{r zone diameter by specimen type}
Panels_zone %>%
  add_count(specimen_type) %>%
  mutate(label = fct_reorder(paste0(specimen_type, " (n=", n, ")"), n)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = label, y = EUCAST_zone)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 17, linetype = "dashed", color = "#898781") +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "#2a78d6", alpha = 0.6, outlier.alpha = 0.4, outlier.size = 0.8) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 50, 10)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "EUCAST disc zone diameter (mm)",
       title = "Zone diameter distribution by specimen type",
       subtitle = "Full dataset; dashed = EUCAST R/I cutoff (17mm)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
```

```{r zone diameter by organism}
Panels_zone %>%
  add_count(organism_group_full) %>%
  mutate(label = fct_reorder(paste0(organism_group_full, " (n=", n, ")"), n)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = label, y = EUCAST_zone)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 17, linetype = "dashed", color = "#898781") +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "#2a78d6", alpha = 0.6, outlier.alpha = 0.4, outlier.size = 0.8) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 50, 10)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "EUCAST disc zone diameter (mm)",
       title = "Zone diameter distribution by organism",
       subtitle = "Small organism counts grouped by genus; dashed = EUCAST R/I cutoff (17mm)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
```

Swab isolates show smaller zone diameters than other specimen types overall. This holds
within every individual organism (not just because swabs have a different organism mix),
though the organism mix does also differ: swabs are proportionally richer in *Klebsiella
pneumoniae* (36% of swabs vs 17% of other specimen types) and leaner in *E. coli* (58% vs
77%), and K. pneumoniae itself tends to run smaller zones than E. coli.

```{r zone diameter swab vs other by organism}
Panels_zone %>%
  filter(organism_group_full %in% c("Escherichia coli", "Klebsiella pneumoniae",
                                     "Klebsiella oxytoca", "Klebsiella variicola",
                                     "Coliform bacilli", "Proteus mirabilis")) %>%
  mutate(specimen_group = if_else(specimen_type == "Swab", "Swab", "All other specimen types"),
         organism_group_full = fct_reorder(organism_group_full, EUCAST_zone)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = organism_group_full, y = EUCAST_zone, fill = specimen_group)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 17, linetype = "dashed", color = "#898781") +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.75, outlier.alpha = 0.4, outlier.size = 0.8,
               position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), width = 0.7) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 50, 10)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Swab" = "#eb6834", "All other specimen types" = "#2a78d6")) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "EUCAST disc zone diameter (mm)", fill = NULL,
       title = "Zone diameter: Swab vs other specimen types, by organism",
       subtitle = "Full dataset; dashed = EUCAST R/I cutoff (17mm)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), legend.position = "top")
```

### Significance testing across specimen types

Zone diameter distributions are skewed and heavy-tailed, vary substantially in spread
across specimen types (the Swab box above is visibly wider than Blood's or Urine's),
and specimen-type group sizes range from n=1 to n>7000 — violating the normality and
equal-variance assumptions a standard one-way ANOVA (a test of **mean** differences)
relies on. A **Kruskal-Wallis test** — the rank-based, non-parametric analogue of
one-way ANOVA, comparing distributions/rank-location rather than means directly — is
used for the omnibus comparison, followed by pairwise **Wilcoxon rank-sum tests** with
Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction for the resulting multiple comparisons. Pairwise
testing is restricted to specimen types with at least 20 samples (Urine, Blood, Swab,
Body Fluid, Sputum, Tissue, Drain/Tube/Other device, Broncho-alveolar Lavage, Fluid),
since comparisons involving the smallest groups (Cerebrospinal Fluid, Synovial Fluid,
Stool, Transport solution, Dialysis fluid, Post mortem swab, Other; all n<=18) aren't
statistically meaningful.

```{r kruskal wallis setup}
specimen_n20 <- Panels_zone %>% count(specimen_type) %>% filter(n >= 20) %>% pull(specimen_type)
Panels_zone_n20 <- Panels_zone %>% filter(specimen_type %in% specimen_n20)

kw_result <- kruskal.test(EUCAST_zone ~ specimen_type, data = Panels_zone_n20)
```

```{r kruskal wallis omnibus table}
tibble(
  Test = "Kruskal-Wallis (omnibus)",
  `Specimen types` = length(specimen_n20),
  n = nrow(Panels_zone_n20),
  `Chi-squared` = round(unname(kw_result$statistic), 1),
  df = unname(kw_result$parameter),
  `p-value` = if (kw_result$p.value < 0.001) "<0.001" else formatC(kw_result$p.value, format = "f", digits = 3)
) %>%
  gt() %>%
  tab_header(title = "Zone diameter across specimen types",
             subtitle = "Omnibus test (specimen types with n>=20)") %>%
  tab_options(table.font.size = px(13))
```

```{r pairwise wilcoxon table}
pw <- pairwise.wilcox.test(Panels_zone_n20$EUCAST_zone, Panels_zone_n20$specimen_type,
                            p.adjust.method = "BH")

pw_wide <- as.data.frame(pw$p.value) %>%
  rownames_to_column("group1")

pw_wide %>%
  gt(rowname_col = "group1") %>%
  tab_header(title = "Pairwise comparisons: zone diameter by specimen type",
             subtitle = "Wilcoxon rank-sum, Benjamini-Hochberg-adjusted p-value") %>%
  tab_stubhead(label = "") %>%
  data_color(columns = -group1,
             fn = function(x) ifelse(is.na(x), "#fcfcfb",
                                      ifelse(x < 0.05, "#f8d7da", "#e8f4ea"))) %>%
  fmt(columns = -group1,
      fns = function(x) ifelse(is.na(x), "",
                                ifelse(x < 0.001, "<0.001", formatC(x, format = "f", digits = 3)))) %>%
  tab_source_note("Green = no significant difference (p>=0.05, BH-adjusted); red = significant difference (p<0.05).") %>%
  tab_options(table.font.size = px(12))
```

Swab is significantly different (adjusted p<0.001) from every other specimen type with
adequate sample size, consistent with the visual pattern above: zone diameters in swabs
are genuinely smaller than in other specimen types, not an artefact of a particular
comparison.

## Predicting discordance by specimen type (Swab, Urine, Blood)

The paired MIC/Disc data (`organisms_of_interest`) only has 613 samples with both an
EUCAST and an Etest result, and 585 of those are Blood (4 Swab, 3 Urine) — too few to
observe Swab/Urine discordance rates directly. Instead, since `EUCAST_interp` is a
deterministic step function of zone diameter, the only real uncertainty is P(Etest = R)
given the zone diameter. A **logistic regression** of Etest result (R vs I) on EUCAST
zone diameter is fit on the 613 paired samples, then applied to every isolate's actual
zone diameter (whether or not it had an Etest done) for the three inclusion-criteria
organisms in Swab, Urine, and Blood, to get an expected (summed-probability) count of
Agreement / I-to-R / R-to-I per specimen type.

```{r logistic model setup}
organisms_of_interest <- organisms_of_interest %>%
  mutate(ETEST_R = ETEST_interp == "R")

logit_model <- glm(ETEST_R ~ EUCAST, data = organisms_of_interest, family = binomial)
```

```{r logistic model diagnostics table}
coefs <- coef(summary(logit_model))
null_model <- glm(ETEST_R ~ 1, data = organisms_of_interest, family = binomial)
mcfadden_r2 <- 1 - as.numeric(logLik(logit_model)) / as.numeric(logLik(null_model))
train_pred <- ifelse(predict(logit_model, type = "response") > 0.5, "R", "I")
train_acc <- mean(train_pred == organisms_of_interest$ETEST_interp)

tibble(Term = rownames(coefs),
       Estimate = round(coefs[, "Estimate"], 3),
       `Std. Error` = round(coefs[, "Std. Error"], 3),
       `z value` = round(coefs[, "z value"], 2),
       `p-value` = if_else(coefs[, "Pr(>|z|)"] < 0.001, "<0.001",
                            formatC(coefs[, "Pr(>|z|)"], format = "f", digits = 3))) %>%
  gt() %>%
  tab_header(title = "Logistic regression: P(Etest = R) ~ EUCAST zone diameter",
             subtitle = paste0("n = ", nrow(organisms_of_interest),
                                "; McFadden R² = ", round(mcfadden_r2, 3),
                                "; AIC = ", round(AIC(logit_model), 1),
                                "; training accuracy = ", scales::percent(train_acc, accuracy = 0.1))) %>%
  tab_options(table.font.size = px(13))
```

```{r logistic model training confusion matrix}
tibble(actual = organisms_of_interest$ETEST_interp, predicted = train_pred) %>%
  count(actual, predicted) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = predicted, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) %>%
  gt(rowname_col = "actual") %>%
  tab_header(title = "Training confusion matrix (threshold = 0.5)",
             subtitle = "Rows = actual Etest result, columns = predicted") %>%
  tab_stubhead(label = "Actual") %>%
  tab_options(table.font.size = px(13))
```

```{r logistic model fit plot}
curve_df <- tibble(EUCAST = seq(min(organisms_of_interest$EUCAST),
                                 max(organisms_of_interest$EUCAST), length.out = 100)) %>%
  mutate(p_R = predict(logit_model, newdata = ., type = "response"))

binned <- organisms_of_interest %>%
  group_by(EUCAST) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), prop_R = mean(ETEST_R), .groups = "drop")

ggplot() +
  geom_point(data = binned, aes(x = EUCAST, y = prop_R, size = n), color = "#2a78d6", alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_line(data = curve_df, aes(x = EUCAST, y = p_R), color = "#d03b3b", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 17, linetype = "dashed", color = "#898781") +
  labs(x = "EUCAST disc zone diameter (mm)", y = "P(Etest = R)", size = "n at zone",
       title = "Logistic fit: P(Etest resistant) by EUCAST zone diameter",
       subtitle = "Points: observed proportion at each zone value (training data, n=613)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
```

**Important caveat on representativeness.** Etest is not ordered on a random sample of
zones: in Blood (the only specimen type with enough paired data to check), 21.9% of
Etest-tested isolates have zone <17mm versus only 8.3% of all Blood isolates — Etest is
preferentially ordered for smaller, more resistant-looking zones (a plausible reflex/
confirmatory-testing pattern). Conditional on zone diameter (which is what the model
uses), this kind of selection does not bias the fitted P(Etest=R | zone) curve itself —
but it does mean the training data is concentrated in the low-zone region and sparse at
higher zones, and the approach assumes the same zone-to-MIC relationship learned
(mostly from Blood) applies unchanged to Swab and Urine, which isn't verified here.

```{r blood MIC tested vs not distribution}
Panels %>%
  filter(
    specimen_type == "Blood",
    organism_or_component == "ESCHERICHIA COLI [202]" |
      (str_detect(organism_or_component, "^KLEBSIELLA") &
         !str_detect(organism_or_component, "AEROGENES")) |
      organism_or_component == "PROTEUS MIRABILIS [338]"
  ) %>%
  mutate(EUCAST_zone = as.numeric(`zone_size_M EUCAST`)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(EUCAST_zone), EUCAST_zone <= 50) %>%
  mutate(mic_tested = if_else(Both == 1, "MIC tested (Etest done)", "MIC not tested")) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = EUCAST_zone, fill = mic_tested)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 17, linetype = "dashed", color = "#898781") +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.55, color = NA) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 40, 5)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("MIC tested (Etest done)" = "#eb6834",
                                "MIC not tested" = "#2a78d6")) +
  labs(x = "EUCAST disc zone diameter (mm)", y = "Density", fill = NULL,
       title = "Blood isolates: zone diameter, MIC-tested vs not",
       subtitle = "E. coli/Klebsiella spp. (excl. aerogenes)/P. mirabilis; dashed = EUCAST R/I cutoff (17mm)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), legend.position = "top")
```

Etest-tested Blood isolates (orange) are visibly shifted toward smaller zone diameters
than untested ones (blue) — the selection-bias pattern behind the caveat above, made
concrete.

```{r calibration check}
insample <- organisms_of_interest %>%
  mutate(p_R = predict(logit_model, type = "response"),
         p_agree = if_else(EUCAST_interp == "R", p_R, 1 - p_R),
         p_I_to_R = if_else(EUCAST_interp == "I", p_R, 0),
         p_R_to_I = if_else(EUCAST_interp == "R", 1 - p_R, 0))

insample %>%
  summarise(n = n(),
            Agreement = sum(p_agree), `I to R` = sum(p_I_to_R), `R to I` = sum(p_R_to_I)) %>%
  mutate(across(c(Agreement, `I to R`, `R to I`), ~ round(., 1))) %>%
  gt() %>%
  tab_header(title = "In-sample calibration check",
             subtitle = "Predicted (summed probabilities) vs actual, on the 613 training samples") %>%
  tab_options(table.font.size = px(13))
```

```{r logistic model final predictions}
pred_counts <- Panels %>%
  filter(
    organism_or_component == "ESCHERICHIA COLI [202]" |
      (str_detect(organism_or_component, "^KLEBSIELLA") &
         !str_detect(organism_or_component, "AEROGENES")) |
      organism_or_component == "PROTEUS MIRABILIS [338]"
  ) %>%
  mutate(EUCAST = as.numeric(`zone_size_M EUCAST`)) %>%
  filter(specimen_type %in% c("Swab", "Urine", "Blood"), !is.na(EUCAST), EUCAST <= 50) %>%
  mutate(
    EUCAST_interp = if_else(EUCAST < 17, "R", "I"),
    p_R = predict(logit_model, newdata = tibble(EUCAST = EUCAST), type = "response"),
    p_agree = if_else(EUCAST_interp == "R", p_R, 1 - p_R),
    p_I_to_R = if_else(EUCAST_interp == "I", p_R, 0),
    p_R_to_I = if_else(EUCAST_interp == "R", 1 - p_R, 0)
  ) %>%
  group_by(specimen_type) %>%
  summarise(n = n(),
            Agreement = sum(p_agree), `I to R` = sum(p_I_to_R), `R to I` = sum(p_R_to_I),
            .groups = "drop")

pred_counts %>%
  mutate(across(c(Agreement, `I to R`, `R to I`), round, 1),
         `Agreement %` = scales::percent(Agreement / n, accuracy = 0.1),
         `I to R %` = scales::percent(`I to R` / n, accuracy = 0.1),
         `R to I %` = scales::percent(`R to I` / n, accuracy = 0.1)) %>%
  select(specimen_type, n, Agreement, `Agreement %`, `I to R`, `I to R %`, `R to I`, `R to I %`) %>%
  gt(rowname_col = "specimen_type") %>%
  tab_header(title = "Predicted discordance by specimen type",
             subtitle = "Expected counts from the fitted logistic model, applied to every isolate's actual zone diameter") %>%
  tab_options(table.font.size = px(13))
```
